Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure.
  - Left-sided decreased hearing and left facial numbness; no clear trigger or exposure identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression.
  - Onset ~3 weeks ago; numbness present most of the time and ongoing; hearing “gone down a bit” on the left.
  - Intermittent left-sided tinnitus with occasional dizziness.
- ENT symptoms (as applicable): throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face), ear/neck symptoms.
  - No dysphagia, no difficulty speaking, no visual changes.
  - No ear discharge, no ear pain reported, no fever, no itchiness in the ear documented.
  - Numbness localized to left peri-auricular area and along left jawline; no facial swelling reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments (including any prior hospital care or injection therapy).
  - Prior history of nasal polyps.
  - Remote history of “labyrinthitis”; no ongoing treatment; no prior hospital care for current issue documented.
- Allergies and current medications (mark missing dose/route/frequency as not documented).
  - Allergy: Latex.
  - Medications:
    - Nasal spray for nasal polyps (name unknown; prescription from past; used as needed; dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Rennies (OTC antacid; used as needed; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Any relevant social context (e.g., accompaniment/supervision).
  - Occupation: Jockey; reduced training due to dizziness with tinnitus.
  - Living situation: initially stated lives alone, later stated lives with partner (conflict noted).
  - No pets.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution (e.g., lips, tongue, uvula, face) if stated.
  - None reported or observed via video.
- Airway/breathing descriptors if stated (e.g., stridor, work of breathing).
  - No breathing difficulty or noisy breathing reported.
- Mental status and associated features (e.g., dizziness, syncope) if stated.
  - Intermittent dizziness associated with tinnitus; no syncope.
- Vitals and examination findings only if mentioned; otherwise note “Not recorded.”
  - Not recorded (video visit; no physical exam performed).
- Presence of another person with the patient (if stated).
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Suspected peripheral facial nerve involvement (possible Bell’s palsy) with concurrent left-sided hearing reduction and intermittent tinnitus/dizziness; requires in-person neurologic and otologic examination.
- Justification: ~3 weeks of unilateral facial numbness around left ear/jawline and decreased hearing; intermittent tinnitus with occasional dizziness; no otorrhea, otalgia, fever, dysphagia, speech or vision problems; clinician expressed preliminary reassurance but recommended urgent same-day exam to confirm diagnosis and exclude other causes.
- Conflict noted: Living situation (lives alone vs lives with partner).

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Same-day face-to-face clinic assessment arranged. Patient instructed to call the support team number (placed in notes) after 5 minutes to be booked into a convenient Central London clinic today.
  - Purpose: neurological examination and otoscopic/ear assessment.
- Specific instructions provided to patient/caregiver:
  - Ensure the appointment is completed today.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Not discussed in transcript.
- Follow-up:
  - In-person evaluation today; further explanation and management (e.g., Bell’s palsy evaluation) to follow after exam.
  - Referrals (ENT/audiology/neurology) not discussed in transcript.
- COVID-19 vaccine suitability:
  - Not discussed.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs or physical exam (cranial nerve VII function/facial weakness, stroke screen).
  - No otoscopy; no bedside hearing tests (Weber/Rinne) or audiometry.
  - No documentation of vesicular rash/ear pain to assess for Ramsay Hunt.
  - No details on noise exposure/trauma, ototoxic medications, or recent infections.
  - Medication names/doses/routes/frequencies incomplete (nasal spray, Rennies).
  - No explicit safety-netting/red-flag advice documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Living situation: “lives alone” vs “lives with partner” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Several inaudible/unclear segments and interruptions; limited by video format; no exam recorded.
